radar.justification: Apache-2.0 spec in a public repository with a CLA, but the founders appoint the TSC and keep a veto.
Bilateral onboarding per platform and founder-controlled governance; no permissionless path.

Beta and Draft labels, mutable releases, examples that do not validate, and a quiet repository since 2026-07-18 (no maintainer comment, review, merge or commit between 2026-07-18 and 2026-10-20; the one maintainer action was closing SEP PR 178 unmerged on 2026-08-09).
Large named partners for feeds, but no published volume and a scaled-back checkout product.
Built around a buyer confirming in session; tokens are one-time and session bound.
Merchant handles chargebacks under card rules and reports adjustments; no dispute protocol.

controlsCells.note: The merchant authenticates the agent with a bearer token agreed out of band, plus a recommended detached Signature and Timestamp with algorithms agreed out of band; the agent verifies webhooks with a shared HMAC secret. No agent identity scheme.
No registry in ACP. Each platform runs its own merchant and partner onboarding, such as ChatGPT's approved-partner application.
The buyer confirms in the agent interface (a product feature). The spec captures marketing consents and 3DS results but no signed purchase consent.
allowance.max_amount and currency on every delegated token; Stripe SPT usage_limits.max_amount.
allowance.merchant_id and allowance.checkout_session_id bind the token to one merchant and one session.
allowance.expires_at, session expires_at and the expired status.
No revoke endpoint in ACP; the agent can revoke a Stripe SPT until it is consumed or resolved. Agents can cancel open sessions.
authentication_required status, authentication_metadata, authentication_result, Delegate Authentication (3DS2) and capabilities.interventions.
Mandatory Idempotency-Key on POST since 2026-04-17, one_time allowance, webhook timestamp window; request Timestamp checks only SHOULD.
Order with permalink_url and order_create and order_update webhooks; no signed receipt.
Order adjustments include refund, return and dispute; the merchant handles chargebacks as merchant of record; no dispute protocol.
risk_signals on complete, RiskSignal entries on Delegate Payment, intent_trace reason codes on cancel, Request-Id.
Merchants can decline any order and agents can cancel sessions; Stripe SPTs can be revoked; no protocol-wide stop.
